The first time I camped properly, with friends, in a planned way and all the equipment was a few years ago.

It would be the first and last time I would go camping with my best friend.

It was the peak of summer and about 18 of us we were due to all meet up for an airsoft weekend at a private site which had about 500 acres available for us to use. As things often go people cancelled, things came up and eventually there was only five left.

The airsoft was cancelled but for the five of us the weekend was still free. So we decided to go anyway. Get out the house. Do some cooking on a fire. Maybe shoot at each other in the cooler night.

It was so hot that weekend. High 30 degree celcius if not 40.

We chose a terrible spot to base ourselves. A raised wide open field. Freshly cut hay stubble, zero cover. It may as well have been the floor of a pizza oven.

One of our number was a tree surgeon (we constantly made lumberjack jokes) and he had a gigantic blue tarpaulin. By gigantic I mean it would have easily been able to cover all of our cars and still provide shade for all of us to sleep under.

Up went the tarp. One end attached to a gigantic wood pole from an old obstacle course. The other end... Well luckily the lumberjack had a tree in his trailer (seemed logical at the time) so we used that to fashion the worlds largest lean to.

I'm pretty sure you could have seen this shelter from space. So I did the honorable thing and put my 3*4M camo net over one end to make it less visible.

We had all brought way too much kit with us. Camp beds, gun cases, changes of clothes, gas grills, camp chairs, I even brought my sleeping bag that was good to minus 30c in case it got cold in the night.

Setting up camp took the entire day. Which in and of itself was kinda the fun part. Working out how to use our equipment, fixing up the shelter, learning how to tie knots effectively, getting out our axes and comparing size, weight and width of the shaft...

We set up a target range for the airsoft guns. The lumberjack also had his air rifle as well so we plunked with that too.

Then when sun down came we setup a braiser. Worried about setting the field on fire we relocated to a first track nearby and scrubbed out a wide area with our newly purchased entrenching tools.

The braiser looked like a solid black Victorian iron chalice in celebration of fire and steaks. And did we have some food. At least two steaks per person, a lamb leg, stir fry vegetables and enough beer to put out the field if it ever did catch ablaze!

The night was still and hot. We decided to go play soldier in the woods which was damp and hotter. Go figure.
So until the early hours we stalked in the dark and shot at shadows, ran through ambushes and sweated enough to dissolve my clothes. I got through about 8 litres of water and still needed more.

I ended up stripping down and passing out on my campbed in the wee hours. Only to be burned awake a few short hours later by a clear blue sky and a bright bright sun. It felt like the tarp was capturing the heat of the morning sun and enhancing it somehow.

I was the only one up, so I picked up a chair, BCB and water and went and found shade. I made coffee in a cool breeze while watching the horizon. Made use of my binoculars to make sight readings to locate myself on a map and generally had a happy quiet time observing nature doing its thing.

Far off I saw a bird of prey. Possibly a Kestrel. I don't know birds so I figured I would say it was a Kestrel. Close to me there was a colony of ants digging out little piles of earth as they expanded outwards.

I was really glad to have done the camp. And sad to go at the end of it. Although at the time I was cursing how much equipment we had and folding that bloody tarpaulin!

Little did I know that this would be my last chance to do this with my best friend. Less than a year later he took his own life. And when I miss him I'll always think of our last, and first, time camping together.

Especially the bit where the cheating bastard had bought night vision and didn't tell us he was using it.

In the end we all agreed to name the campsite after him. It's where I go when I want to remember one of the best times I had with him.
